props.title: Is Paris Burning?
props.initialSlug: WW2 epic: Will Nazis destroy occupied Paris?

sections.content: Is Paris Burning? stands as a monumental war epic chronicling the liberation of Paris in August 1944. Director René Clément assembled an incredible international cast including Jean-Paul Belmondo, Charles Boyer, and Orson Welles to recreate the tense final days of Nazi occupation. The film's title comes from Hitler's infamous question to his generals, demanding to know if his orders to destroy Paris had been carried out. Shot in stark black and white by Marcel Grignon, the film masterfully blends actual wartime footage with dramatic recreations, setting a template later used in films like The Longest Day (1962) and A Bridge Too Far (1977).

sections.content: The film's documentary-style approach influenced later WWII resistance films like Army of Shadows (1969) and The Sorrow and the Pity (1969). Gore Vidal and Francis Ford Coppola's screenplay navigates multiple storylines, following resistance fighters, German officers, and civilians as their fates intertwine during the uprising. The film's attention to historical accuracy is remarkable - many scenes were filmed in actual locations where events occurred, and several real resistance fighters served as technical advisors. SUBHEAD: Impact on War Cinema

Is Paris Burning? marked a shift in how occupation and resistance were portrayed on screen. Unlike earlier, more propagandistic war films, it presented a complex view of collaboration and resistance, influencing later works like Lacombe, Lucien (1974) and Au Revoir les Enfants (1987). The film's massive street scenes, involving thousands of extras, set a standard for historical recreation that wouldn't be matched until Saving Private Ryan (1998) and Dunkirk (2017).
